findings.reason: the control must be stated as the behaviour being removed (the non-seeding launch's strip), or a node whose correct fix lives at the call sites is blocked on a control that cannot fail, and its measure rests on a suite that would also pass on the unfixed code.
findings.text: §11's negative control is "with the untouched-prompt return restored for a launch that seeds no server, the first test fails", which falsifies only a fix made inside `with_anchored_edit_instruction`; the fix must also reach the launch caller, since the caller never invokes the owner for a non-seeding launch (`reckon/_backends.py:3117`), so a node that strips at the call sites delivers the endpoint while the named return stays exactly as it is and the control passes vacuously — the node then cannot show its guard fires and would have to report a control it could not make fail
